children: Microsoft (MSFT) Q1 revenue $92.28B (+18.8% YoY); net income $36.63B; diluted EPS $4.92. Microsoft Cloud revenue $63.9B (+30%); Azure revenue accelerated 48% YoY, above guidance.
Microsoft (MSFT) is selling $25B in debt — $23B fixed-rate, $2B floating — to fund capex, acquisitions and refinancing; offering expected to close Nov. 4.
Microsoft priced $25B of unsecured senior debt across 10 maturities to fund AI infrastructure and related capital spending, per the filing.
Microsoft (MSFT) will adopt a unified opt-out for publishers to block their content from future AI model training, effective February 1, 2027; it covers future training only.
Microsoft (MSFT) reported strong cloud performance, disciplined cash-flow management, and rising enterprise adoption of Copilot; leadership credited for overseeing cloud and AI expansion.
Microsoft (MSFT) CFO Amy Hood said the company may seek external funding when markets are favorable and has used lease financing to support infrastructure expansion.
Microsoft says a new rule affects only future model training, won’t change page access; content remains scrappable by default, and publishers can opt out of use in Microsoft-generated responses.
The New York Times sued OpenAI and Microsoft over alleged unpaid use of its articles in AI training data. Microsoft is named as a defendant; companies dispute the claim via a copyright defense.
Microsoft (MSFT) five-year CDS widened to 55 bps from 47 bps, remaining the lowest among Big Tech, indicating comparatively lower market-priced credit risk for traders.
Microsoft expanded its cloud, data and AI deal with Estée Lauder, deploying Copilot to 14,000+ office employees to automate tasks and support marketing, commerce, supply chain and R&D workflows.
